purpose: Tier transitions as machine-readable state. A rule that claimed a tier and lost it used to be able to record that only as prose in its source comment, which is how QA-JV-101 came to carry three stacked and mutually contradictory provenance notes. A transition that is not in this file did not happen, and one that is in this file must end at the rule's LIVE tier — checked field by field on every `npm run rules:promotion:check`.
whyNotNewTierValues: The obvious fix — adding `demoted` / `deprecated` / `experimental` to the `Tier` union — was rejected on blast radius, not taste. `tier` is read in roughly fifteen non-rule modules (tier-policy score caps, scan-pipeline filters, explain, catalog, triage, plugins, doctor, conformity, registry-census). A new value that falls through unhandled in any of them changes finding behaviour silently, which in a tool whose entire claim is measured trust is the one failure mode that must not ship. Recording history does not touch the tier algebra, so nothing about what a scan reports can move.
whatThisIsNot: Not an authority to promote. A record whose final transition says `core` does not make a rule core — the registry and `docs/CORE-CERTIFICATION.json` do that. This file is checked AGAINST the live registry, so it cannot grant a tier; it can only fail when it disagrees with one.

transitions.reason: n=35 with zero observed false positives clears the 10% Wilson ceiling at 9.89%. Adjudicated row by row against pinned corpus commits; four candidate rows were retracted as orphans citing a line one above the annotation rather than quietly dropped.

Demoted for an unsubstantiated claim. 0% observed over a thin sample is a wide interval, not a small one, and a rule cannot be core on a premise. Per-rule interval is re-derived live in src/rules/tier-evidence.ts rather than committed here.

Re-earned in two batches, and the sequence is the point: 32 (10.72%) -> 34 (10.15%) -> 35 (9.89%). The first batch's verdict file reads as a refusal on its own; the second, from a sweep run after corpus-sample.ts was corrected to clone the pinned ref instead of the default branch, is what cleared the ceiling. Reading only the first batch is how this promotion was wrongly reported as fabricated.
